Beginner.learningGoal: Define a protocol, conform types to it and add behaviour with extensions.
gotchas: A protocol extension method that is not a requirement is statically dispatched
Protocols cannot store properties, only declare them
Conforming in an extension must still satisfy every requirement
goodSolutionShows: A small protocol with two conforming types and a function accepting the protocol
Protocol extension supplying a default implementation
Extensions to add computed properties instead of subclassing
shapeHints: notification channels that format a message differently
a Describable protocol with a default description

Intermediate.learningGoal: Use protocol extensions with constraints and default implementations, understanding static vs dynamic dispatch.
gotchas: A default implementation not declared as a requirement is not overridden through the protocol type
Conditional conformance: extension Array: P where Element: P
Ambiguity when two extensions with overlapping constraints both apply
goodSolutionShows: Requirement declared in the protocol so dispatch is dynamic
shapeHints: a Validator protocol with composed validators
extending Sequence with a statistic helper only for numeric elements
a Pricing protocol with default discount logic

Advanced.learningGoal: Design protocol-oriented abstractions with protocol composition, existentials and conditional conformance.
gotchas: Operations on an array of any-boxed values dispatch to each element's own conformance, so tests need elements of different concrete types
Equality across heterogeneous existentials needs an explicit rule such as comparing the concrete type first, and tests must cover equal and unequal pairs of different types
A default provided through a constrained extension applies only where the constraint holds, so tests need elements that satisfy it and elements that fall back
goodSolutionShows: Conditional conformance such as Equatable for a generic wrapper
some used for return types and any only where heterogeneity is needed
Tests proving behaviour through the protocol, not concrete types
Retroactive conformance avoided, or isolated, for types the module does not own
Self-requirement protocols used as existentials only through any
shapeHints: a Plugin pipeline of heterogeneous stages
Comparable for a wrapper of Comparable values
a heterogeneous collection of Renderable items with constrained helpers

Expert.learningGoal: Combine protocol composition, existentials and constrained extensions into an extensible design, controlling which implementation wins and testing it through the protocol.
gotchas: Two constrained extensions that provide the same method are ambiguous when both apply, and the more constrained one wins only when it is strictly more specific
A conforming type's method with the same name as a defaulted non-requirement is called through the concrete type but not through the protocol type
Operations on a collection of existentials can only use the protocol's requirements, so extra behaviour needs a requirement or an optional capability protocol checked with as?
goodSolutionShows: Capability protocols checked with as? and tested with conforming and non-conforming types
Behaviour verified through the existential type rather than the concrete types
Defaults declared as requirements so overrides are honoured through the protocol
shapeHints: a plugin system where some plugins also conform to a Configurable capability
validator composition with a general all-of and a specialised path for String elements
a Formatter protocol whose collection extension picks a specialised path for strings
